exposure: Maternal Chlamydia trachomatis (C. trachomatis) screening and treatment status during pregnancy
cohort: Pregnant women attending first-time gynecological-obstetric consultations at the National Institute of Perinatology in 2018, and their infants, were included in the study.
finding: Undetected maternal C. trachomatis infection during pregnancy significantly increases the risk of neonatal infection and subsequent perinatal pneumonia, despite a low observed mother-to-child transmission rate in treated positive mothers.
